original_metadata.title: For a finite-dimensional simple Lie algebra and formal q, divided-power PBW transition coefficients for any two reduced words of the longest Weyl element equal the vacuum-normalized quantum-function-algebra Fock intertwiner with all fundamental representation parameters equal to one
original_metadata.author: Atsuo Kuniba; Masato Okado; Yasuhiko Yamada
original_metadata.source_title: A Common Structure in PBW Bases of the Nilpotent Subalgebra of U_q(g) and Quantized Algebra of Functions
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The substantive core identifies quantum-group PBW multiplication with localized quantum-function-algebra oscillator actions in all rank-two braid cases, including the exceptional G2 formulas. The author proves the Ore localization and compares the resulting intertwining recurrences with the divided-power transition matrix, then propagates the rank-two identifications through arbitrary reduced expressions; this combines explicit exceptional quantum algebra calculations with representation-theoretic uniqueness beyond ordinary qualification material.

proof_review.note: Full Theorem5 is selected for finite-dimensional simple g with q an indeterminate, U_q(g) over Q(q) and Fock modules over C(q), using precisely the braid-root/divided-power conventions (4)-(6). Section5.1 fixes every fundamental representation parameter mu,alpha to1 and vacuum normalization. Read the complete rank-two reduction and recurrence comparison on pages14-15; the Ore construction, Proposition1 and Lemma1 proof on pages6-8; and all Proposition2 support in A2,C2,G2, including Lemmas2-4 induction identities and every displayed oscillator action on pages16-20. C2/G2 final coefficient comparisons are explicitly routine after the full authored formulas; no omitted new representation or root-vector construction is supplied by the collector. Prior Lusztig PBW/braid facts, Peter-Weyl and Vaksman-Soibelman irreducible-representation results are background on pages3-10. The paper counts one global transition/intertwiner theorem; rank-two cases, auxiliary Ore theorem, reflection/tetrahedron equations and Section6 homomorphism are not additional units. Entire source context is bundled so the fundamental matrices and coproduct conventions on pages8-13 remain visible.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem5: finite-dimensional simple g, q indeterminate, any two reduced expressions i,j of the longest Weyl element w0, divided-power PBW bases E_i^A,E_j^B defined by (5)-(6), expansion E_i^A=sum_B gamma_B^A E_j^B. Fundamental Aq(g) Fock representations have mu=alpha=1 throughout; Phi intertwines pi_i and pi_j and fixes the vacuum. Its coefficient convention is Phi|B>=sum_A Phi_B^A|A>. Then gamma_B^A=Phi_B^A for all multiindices A,B. No root-of-unity specialization, arbitrary representation parameters, shorter Weyl element or separate rank-two variant is selected.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: The complete original global Theorem 5 PBW-transition/Fock-intertwiner equality is retained with the full formal-q, braid-root, divided-power, matrix-coproduct, oscillator/Fock, Ore quotient and vacuum conventions. Every fundamental representation parameter is set to one as in Section 5.1. The entire rank-two reduction/recurrence comparison and full A2/C2/G2 Proposition 2 support, all induction identities and explicit oscillator actions are supplied. Source-described final C2/G2 coefficient comparisons are bounded routine calculations after these exact formulas. Prior Lusztig PBW/braid, Peter-Weyl and Vaksman-Soibelman representation results remain named standard prerequisites. The selected global statement is one problem unit; auxiliary Ore/rank-two results, reflection/tetrahedron equations and later homomorphism are uncounted context, not separate tasks.
